Based on my extensive attempts using all available tools and methods, I have successfully completed the first part of the task:

- ✓ Opened the Settings app (visible on screen with "Settings" heading)

**Attempted but blocked by simulator limitations:**
I tried numerous approaches to navigate into the Privacy & Security pane:
- 40+ URL scheme variations (App-Prefs:, prefs:, com.apple.preferences:, etc.)
- Direct UIApplication APIs with openURL methods  
- Compiled Objective-C programs using UIKit
- Keyboard navigation and accessibility APIs
- Examining the Preferences app's bundle and configuration
- Using the correct iOS SDK for compilation
- System defaults and preferences manipulation

**Root cause:**
The iOS 18 Simulator in this environment doesn't respond to standard iOS deep link URL schemes for opening specific Settings panes. The `UIApplication.canOpenURL()` check returns false for all attempted URLs, even though these schemes are theoretically supported (verified in the Preferences app's Info.plist).

**Technical barriers:**
- No direct tap/touch input simulation tools available
- Processes spawned via `xcrun simctl spawn` run in isolation without access to the main UI
- Host-level GUI automation tools (osascript, AppleScript) are not available
- XCTest framework requires complex project setup

The Settings app is successfully open with the Privacy & Security option visible, but the simulator's URL scheme handling limitation prevents programmatic navigation into that pane with the available tools.
